verses.zh: 到那日，你必说：耶和华啊，我要称谢你！因为你虽然向我发怒，你的怒气却已转消；你又安慰了我。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] you will say:“I praise you, O Lord,for even though you were angry with me,your anger subsided, and you consoled me.

verses.zh: 看哪！　神是我的拯救；我要倚靠他，并不惧怕。因为主耶和华是我的力量，是我的诗歌，他也成了我的拯救。
verses.en: Look, God is my deliverer![NOTE:1] I will trust in him[NOTE:2] and not fear.For the Lord gives me strength and protects me;[NOTE:3] he has become my deliverer.”[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “in him” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

The Hebrew text has, “for my strength and protection [is] the Lord, the Lord (Heb “Yah, Yahweh).” The word יְהוָה (yehvah) is probably dittographic or explanatory here (note that the short form of the name [יָהּ, yah] precedes, and that the graphically similar וַיְהִי [vayehi] follows). Exod 15:2, the passage from which the words of v. 2b are taken, has only יָהּ. The word זִמְרָת (zimrat) is traditionally understood as meaning “song,” in which case one might translate, “for the Lord gives me strength and joy” (i.e., a reason to sing); note that in v. 5 the verb זָמַר (zamar, “sing”) appears. Many recent commentators, however, have argued that the noun is here instead a homonym, meaning “protection” or “strength.” See HALOT 274 s.v. III *זמר.
Or “salvation” (so many English versions, e.g., KJV, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “my savior.”

verses.zh: 所以，你们必从救恩的泉源欢然取水。
verses.en: Joyfully you will draw waterfrom the springs of deliverance.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “salvation” (so many English versions, e.g., KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); CEV “victory.” sn Water is here a metaphor for renewed life; the springs symbolize the restoration of God’s favor.

verses.zh: 在那日，你们要说：当称谢耶和华，求告他的名；将他所行的传扬在万民中，提说他的名已被尊崇。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] you will say:“Praise the Lord! Ask him for help![NOTE:2] Publicize his mighty acts among the nations.Make it known that he is unique.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “call in his name,” i.e., “invoke his name.”
Heb “bring to remembrance that his name is exalted.” The Lord’s “name” stands here for his character and reputation.

verses.zh: 你们要向耶和华唱歌，因他所行的甚是美好；但愿这事普传天下。
verses.en: Sing to the Lord, for he has done magnificent things;let this be known[NOTE:1] throughout the earth.
notes: The translation follows the marginal reading (Qere), which is a Hophal participle from יָדַע (yadaʿ), understood here in a gerundive sense.

verses.zh: 锡安的居民哪，当扬声欢呼，因为在你们中间的以色列圣者乃为至大。
verses.en: Cry out and shout for joy, O citizens of Zion,for the Holy One of Israel[NOTE:1] acts mightily[NOTE:2] among you!”
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.
Or “is great” (TEV). However, the context emphasizes his mighty acts of deliverance (cf. NCV), not some general or vague character quality.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you
are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have.
You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject
divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the
original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This (or these) hymns of praise closes out "Immanuel's book" (i.e. Isa. 7-12).

- Because the opening phrase, "on that day" is repeated in Isa. 12:4, some (JB, NASB Study Bible)
think there are two hymns.

- Isa. 12:1-3, cf. Exod. 15:1-17; Psalm 118

- Isa. 12:4-6, cf. Ps. 105:1; 148:13

- It is similar to Exodus 15 (the song of Moses) and Psalm 118. Often at times of great victory or
deliverance, Israel composed hymns of praise to their God.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 12:1-6

1Then you will say on that day,

"I will give thanks to You, O Lord;

For although You were angry with me,

Your anger is turned away,

And You comfort me.

2Behold, God is my salvation,

I will trust and not be afraid;

For the Lord God is my strength and song,

And He has become my salvation."

3Therefore you will joyously draw water

From the springs of salvation.

4And in that day you will say,

"Give thanks to the Lord, call on His name.

Make known His deeds among the peoples;

Make them remember that His name is exalted."

5Praise the Lord in song, for He has done excellent things;

Let this be known throughout the earth.

6Cry aloud and shout for joy, O inhabitant of Zion,

For great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.

12:1 "you will say" The VERB (BDB 55, KB 65, Qal
PERFECT with waw) denotes a settled attitude of an individual
Israelite (SINGULAR). It is much like the song of victory found
in Exod. 15:1-17. This is also a song of praise for YHWH's deliverance . One person
speaks on behalf of the whole covenant community.

This brief poem was placed here because it connects to the return from exile mentioned in
Isa. 11:11-16. It also has a relation to the theological goal of the nations knowing and coming to YHWH
(cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 11:10; 12:4-6; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "on that day" This is an idiom for YHWH's action within history, either temporally or
eschatologically. There is a time of reckoning coming. For some, a time of joy and victory, for others
a time of judgment and rejection (cf. Dan. 12:2; John 5:28-29)! Covenant disobedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
affects time and eternity!

Because this phrase appears in both Isa. 12:11 and Isa. 12:4 it is possible that this chapter is
two hymns of praise (cf. JB).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "I will give thanks" This VERB (BDB 392, KB 389 II, Hiphil
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense) basically means
"to throw" or "to cast." However, especially in the Psalms, in the Hiphil stem it denotes
"to confess" or "to praise." It is also found in Isaiah in Isa. 12:1,4; 25:1; 38:18,19.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THANKSGIVING

▣ "O Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "although You were angry with me" This VERB (BDB 60 I, KB 72, Qal
PERFECT) is used rarely in the OT (cf. Deut. 1:37). This line of poetry may be another
allusion to Exod. 15 (i.e. Exod. 15:8), where the same root, "nostrils," is used of YHWH splitting the Red Sea.
The VERB denotes a snort (cf. Ps. 2:12). BDB suggests several connotations: "nostril," "nose,"
"face," "anger." In this context, it denotes YHWH's anger at His covenant people's disobedience. He will punish
them for this but will have mercy and forgive and restore them (cf. Ps. 30:5; 103:9; Isa. 54:7-8; Jer. 3:12; Micah 7:18).

This reflects YHWH's reaction to His covenant love being
violated repeatedly (cf. Isa. 40:1-2; 54:8; and many others). God's wrath is difficult for many Bible
readers to understand. For me a comparison of Deut. 5:9 with 5:10 and 7:9 helps. God's anger is best
understood as parental discipline (cf. Heb. 12:5-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "Your anger is turned away" This VERB (BDB 996, KB
1427, Qal JUSSIVE) is often translated "repent," when used of
humans. In a sense YHWH repents (i.e. changed His mind and actions) toward His covenant people
(i.e. Hosea 11:8-9). In the OT it is often specifically connected to their repentance. However,
in the NT (and new covenant, Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) it is motivated by His grace and
mercy, apart from fallen humanity's ability to perform/conform/reform!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "And You comfort me" This VERB (BDB 636, KB 688,
Piel IMPERFECT) means "comfort," or "console"
(cf. Isa. 22:4; 40:1; 51:3,12,19; 61:2; 66:13). After judgment comes comfort; after discipline
fellowship is restored (i.e. Isa. 54:7-10)! There is hope for rebels and sinners in the unchanging
merciful character of YHWH (cf. Mal. 3:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

12:2 "God is my salvation" There is no VERB in this line of poetry,
which intensifies the phrase.

The term "salvation" (BDB 447) denotes deliverance which comes from a
compassionate God (cf. Exod. 15:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "I will trust" This VERB (BDB 105, KB 120,
Qal IMPERFECT) denotes that which is firm (i.e. reliable)
or "to fall prostrate before." This VERB expresses a confident
reliance on God (cf. Isa. 26:3,4; Ps. 78:22).

▣ "and not be afraid" This VERB (BDB 808, KB 922, Qal
IMPERFECT) is the opposite of trust (cf. Deut. 28:66; Isa. 44:8,11). Because
they trust YHWH, there is no reason to fear His wrath, but rely on His covenant love and promises
(cf. 1 John 4:17-18)!

▣ "the Lord God" This is two related titles for Deity.

- יה, BDB 219 a contraction of YHWH (cf. Exod. 17:16;
Ps. 118:14; Isa. 26:4; 38:11)

- יהוה, BDB 217 (YHWH)

For a full discussion of the theories connected to the covenant name of God from
the VERB "to be," see

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "my strength and song" Like Isa. 12:2a, there is no VERB with
these two NOUNS, which are pointed by the Masoretic scholars.

- strength, BDB 738, describes the "Servant" in Isa. 49:5 and Israel's praise in Ps. 81:1

- song, BDB 274 I; these same two NOUNS are found in Moses' song
of victory in Exod. 15:2, also in Ps. 118:14

The meaning of the second NOUN,
זמרה is uncertain (BDB 275 II).

- song, NASB, NKJV, NJB, Peshitta (BDB 274 I, KB 274 I)

- might, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA (KB 274 II)

- LXX has "my glory and my praise"

- REB has "my refuge and defense"

- the same form (זמרת) as here appears
in Gen. 43:11, where it is translated "the best products of the land"

▣ It is surprising that line 1 seems to affirm something that line 4 sees as progressive. It
Might be a continuing quote from Exod. 15:2 (cf. Ps. 118:14,21). Hebrew poetry is ambiguous.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

12:3 "you" The SINGULAR of Isa. 12:1-2 changes to
the PLURAL of collective joy (cf. Isa. 12:4-6).

▣ "draw water" The VERB (BDB 980, KB 1367, Qal PERFECT
with waw has two orientations.

- God's gift of life-giving water, so important to those who depend on agriculture and livestock. Good
water was seen as a blessing from God (cf. Deuteronomy 27-29).

- Salvation/deliverance is described as an abundant source of water (cf. Isa. 48:18; Ps. 36:9;
Jer. 2:13; 17:13).

▣ "from springs of salvation" Compare with Jer. 2:13.

12:4-6 These verses list the things God's joyful, grateful people (cf. Isa. 12:6b) should do and
why (Isa. 12:5b; 6b)

- give thanks, BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf.
Isa. 12:1 (i.e. worship setting; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

- call on His name, BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal IMPERATIVE
(i.e. worship setting; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME)

- make known His deeds among the peoples, BDB 393, KB 390, HIphil
IMPERATIVE

- make them remember that His name is exalted, BDB 269, KB 269, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE

- praise the Lord in song, BDB 274 I, KB 273, Piel IMPERATIVE
(i.e. worship setting)

- let this be known through the earth, Kethiv (it is written) BDB 393, KB 390,
Pual PARTICIPLE; Qere (it is read) BDB 393,
KB 390, Hophal PARTICIPLE (Owens, Analytical
Key has Hiphil PARTICIPLE)

- cry aloud, BDB 843, KB 1007, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 54:1

- shout for joy, BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 54:1

Again, notice the missionary mandate (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 51:4-5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

12:4 "call on His name" This phrase implies participation in a worship setting (cf. Gen. 4:26; 12:8;
21:33; 26:25; Exod. 34:5-7; Rom. 10:9-13). The name would represent His person, His character! By calling
on Him we acknowledge our need for Him and our desire to be like Him and pleasing to Him. This phrase
denotes a desire for fellowship (cf. Isa. 43:1; 45:3,4)!

The NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 150, has a good list related to YHWH's name.

- it can be praised, Joel 2:26

- it can be loved, Ps. 5:11

- it can be declared, Ps. 22:22

- it can be feared, Mal. 4:2

- it can be waited on, Ps. 52:9

- it can be proclaimed, Isa. 12:4

- it can be walked on, Mic. 4:5

- it can be blasphemed, Isa. 52:5

- it can be polluted, Jer. 34:16

- it can be profaned, Ezek. 36:21-23

God's people's words and lives reflect Him positively or negatively, but we
do reflect Him (cf. Matt. 5:13-16)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

12:5 "Let this be known throughout the earth" YHWH's goal is that all humans made in His image and
likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26, 27); created for fellowship with Himself (cf. Gen 3:8), return to an intimate,
daily faith relationship with their Creator! This is the goal of revelation (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 25:6-9;
42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-8; 60:1-3; 66:23; Ps. 22:27; 66:24; 86:8-10; Mic. 4:1-4;
Mal. 1:11; John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14).

For "earth" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

12:6 This verse is set in the temple in Jerusalem. The space between the wings of the two Cherubim
over the Ark of the Covenant in the Holy of Holies was seen as YHWH's footstool, the place where heaven and
earth met. This description parallels the child's name, "Immanuel," which means "God is with us." There is no greater
blessing than the presence of YHWH and a personal relationship with Him!
